test_tooling_constraint.javascript: remotion-composer has NO test runner (devDependencies: @types/react, typescript only). Adding jest/vitest would be a dependency addition, which the owner excluded unless proven necessary.
test_tooling_constraint.chosen_strategy: Render-based golden/contrast tests driven from the existing pytest suite via `npx remotion still` (already installed) plus Pillow (already a Python dependency). Zero new dependencies; asserts the real render path.
test_tooling_constraint.python: pytest with tests/contracts/ conventions; tests/conftest.py blocks outbound sockets (loopback allowed), so all tests must stay local.

findings.title: StatCard subtitle unreadable on light themes
findings.root_cause: Explainer passes stat/subtitle/accentColor/backgroundColor but never `color`, so StatCard falls back to its dark-theme default #FFFFFF. The theme object already holds textColor.
findings.evidence: projects/million-billion-trillion/snapshots (pre-fix sc2 still): white subtitle on #F9FAFB field.
findings.smallest_fix: In Explainer's stat_card branch pass color={textColor} (textColor is already computed on the line above as cut.color || theme.textColor). No component API change.
findings.backward_compat_risk: cosmetic-low: on flat-motion-graphics subtitle #FFFFFF -> #F8FAFC (imperceptible); on anime-ghibli #FFFFFF -> #F0E6D3 (slight warm tint, arguably the theme's intent).
tests: light-theme render assert: subtitle pixel contrast vs background >= 4.5:1
dark-theme golden: flat-motion-graphics stat_card frame hash stable or contrast unchanged

findings.title: KPIGrid cannot render decimals or exact >=1000 values
findings.root_cause: displayValue = Math.round(metric.value * countProgress) forces integers; formatDisplayValue abbreviates >=1e3 as '31.7K' and >=1e6 as 'M'. No prop controls decimals or abbreviation. formatDisplayValue is local to KPIGrid (not shared).
findings.class: implementation bug (missing capability) + documentation mismatch (SCENE_TYPES.md implies arbitrary metrics)
findings.evidence: sc4 rendered '12 days / 32 years / 31.7K years' against approved 11.6 / 31.7 / 31,700.
findings.smallest_fix: Add two optional Metric fields - `decimals?: number` and `abbreviate?: boolean` (default true) - plus optional grid-level defaults; when decimals is set use toFixed(decimals) and thousands separators via toLocaleString; when abbreviate is false skip the K/M branch. Defaults reproduce today's output exactly.
findings.backward_compat_risk: none when the new fields are omitted (identical output); additive props only.
tests: unit-ish render assert: metrics [11.6,'days'],[31.7,'years'],[31700,'years'] with decimals/abbreviate produce '11.6 days','31.7 years','31,700 years'
default-path golden: existing integer metrics unchanged, 31700 still renders '31.7K' when abbreviate omitted

findings.title: SectionTitle / StatReveal / HeroTitle hardcode near-white text
findings.root_cause: Colour constants baked into the components; Explainer forwards only accentColor/position, so no caller can correct them.
findings.evidence: sc1 overlay 'MEASURED IN SECONDS' near-white on light field; HeroTitle rejected at scene_plan for the same reason (decision d11).
findings.smallest_fix: Add optional colour props (textColor / subtitleColor / titleColor) defaulting to the CURRENT constants, then have Explainer forward theme-derived values only when the resolved background is light (the existing isLightColor helper in Explainer.tsx). Dark themes keep byte-identical output.
findings.backward_compat_risk: zero for dark themes with the light-only forwarding; HIGH if theme colours were forwarded unconditionally - HeroTitle's cyan/purple would become theme accents and visibly change every existing hero_title (e.g. the zero-key demo world-in-numbers).
findings.dark_projects_affected: no (with the recommended light-only forwarding); yes if unconditional forwarding is chosen instead
tests: light-theme contrast assertions for all three components
dark-theme golden hash for HeroTitle/SectionTitle/StatReveal must be byte-identical to pre-fix

findings.title: ComparisonCard per-side colours not forwarded
findings.root_cause: Explainer forwards leftLabel/rightLabel/leftValue/rightValue/title/backgroundColor/textColor but drops cut.leftColor and cut.rightColor, so component defaults always win.
findings.evidence: sc3 right value rendered #10B981, outside the premium-minimalist accents; owner accepted the deviation (d18).
findings.smallest_fix: Forward leftColor={cut.leftColor ?? theme.primaryColor} and rightColor={cut.rightColor ?? theme.accentColor}? - NOTE: defaulting to theme colours changes existing output. Safer minimal fix: forward only when the cut supplies them (cut.leftColor && {leftColor: cut.leftColor}), leaving defaults untouched.
findings.backward_compat_risk: zero with the pass-through-only variant; medium if defaults are re-pointed at the theme (every existing comparison scene changes colour).
tests: render with explicit leftColor/rightColor and assert the value pixels match
render without them and assert output identical to pre-fix golden

findings.title: Subtitle style: schema vocabulary does not reach the renderer, and a schema-valid value crashes the resolver
findings.root_cause: Three separate mismatches. (a) _build_subtitle_style reads ASS keys (primary_color, outline_color, back_color, alignment, margin_v, outline_width, border_style) while the schema defines color, outline_color, background, position, max_words_per_line - so color/position are silently dropped and hex values are emitted where ASS needs &HAABBGGRR. (b) _resolve_subtitle_style does edit_decisions['subtitles']['style'].items(), but the schema types `style` as a STRING ('sentence'|'word-by-word'|'karaoke') - reproduced: AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'items'. (c) FontSize is interpreted by libass against the SRT->ASS script height (288 lines), so schema font_size is not pixels at 1080p - 42 rendered ~157px.
findings.class: schema mismatch + implementation bug + documentation mismatch
findings.evidence: First burn produced oversized, vertically-centred captions obscuring scene content (defect C6); AttributeError reproduced directly against the schema-valid shape.
findings.smallest_fix: Add a mapping layer in video_compose: translate the schema's subtitles fields (color->primary_color with hex->&HBBGGRR conversion, background->back_color, position->alignment, max_words_per_line passthrough) and scale font_size by playres (font_size * 288/height) unless an explicit ASS key is supplied; make _resolve_subtitle_style accept `style` as either a string (display style) or a legacy dict, reading sibling fields for styling. Keep explicit ASS keys working as the highest-priority override.
findings.backward_compat_risk: medium-visible: projects that today pass ASS-style dicts under subtitles.style keep working (explicit override retained), but any project that relied on the silently-dropped schema fields will now actually get them - captions will change size/colour/position, for the better. This is a public contract clarification and must be called out in the fix note.
findings.dark_projects_affected: yes - any project that burns subtitles through the schema fields will change appearance (currently those fields do nothing).
tests: unit: schema-valid subtitles block -> expected force_style string (colour converted, alignment 2, scaled FontSize)
unit: subtitles.style as string no longer raises
unit: explicit ASS keys still win
render: burned frame has captions in the bottom third and no overlap with the centre band

findings.title: Slideshow-risk check silently disabled by a scene_plan shape mismatch
findings.root_cause: _render passes inputs['scene_plan'] straight through, and the compose-director skill passes the scene_plan ARTIFACT ({version, style_playbook, scenes[], metadata}). score_slideshow_risk expects a LIST of scenes; iterating the dict yields its keys (strings) -> 'str' object has no attribute 'get'. The exception is swallowed by a bare `except Exception` and logged as a warning, so the governance check silently never runs.
findings.class: implementation bug + validation gap (the swallow hides it)
findings.evidence: Reproduced exactly: AttributeError at `types = Counter(s.get('type','unknown') for s in scenes)`. Confirmed the same call succeeds when given scene_plan['scenes'].
findings.smallest_fix: Normalise at the boundary: `scenes = scene_plan.get('scenes', []) if isinstance(scene_plan, dict) else (scene_plan or [])`. Optionally downgrade the bare except to log the exception type and add it to `warnings` so a broken governance check is visible rather than silent.
findings.backward_compat_risk: behavioural: the slideshow gate starts actually running. A project whose plan scores 'fail' would now be BLOCKED at compose where it previously rendered. That is the intended governance behaviour but it can stop existing pipelines - must be flagged to the owner before enabling.
findings.dark_projects_affected: not theme-related, but any existing project can be affected by the gate becoming live
tests: unit: artifact-dict input scores identically to list input, no exception
unit: the canonical million-billion-trillion scene_plan scores and returns a verdict
unit: a deliberately slideshow-y plan produces verdict fail (gate still works)

findings.title: Overlay timing keys fail late as a NaN Sequence error
files: remotion-composer/src/Explainer.tsx (Overlay interface uses in_seconds/out_seconds; overlay Sequence ~line 829)
tools/analysis/composition_validator.py (validates cuts + audio only - no overlay checks)
findings.root_cause: The Overlay contract requires in_seconds/out_seconds. Any other key (e.g. start_seconds) yields undefined -> from=NaN and Remotion throws mid-render: 'The from prop of a sequence must be finite, but got NaN.' composition_validator inspects cuts and audio but never overlays, so nothing catches it earlier.
findings.class: validation gap (contract is correct; enforcement is missing)
findings.evidence: Reproduced during this run - the first still render aborted with the NaN Sequence TypeError; composition_validator had reported valid=true on the same file.
findings.smallest_fix: Add an overlay check to composition_validator: each overlay must have numeric finite in_seconds/out_seconds with out > in, a known `type`, and (for section_title/stat_reveal/hero_title) a `text`. Emit a targeted error naming the correct keys when start_seconds/end_seconds are present.
findings.backward_compat_risk: low-additive: projects with malformed overlays start failing validation, but they already fail at render. No schema change.
tests: validator rejects overlay with start_seconds/end_seconds and names in_seconds/out_seconds
validator rejects out<=in and non-numeric values
validator still passes the frozen baseline composition

findings.title: Canonical cuts cannot carry component props
files: tools/analysis/composition_validator.py (validates a composition JSON by path)
findings.root_cause: Two parallel contracts exist: the canonical editorial artifact (strict) and the Remotion composition JSON (scene props). _remotion_render consumes the composition shape, but the canonical artifact has no declared field recording WHICH props file produced the render, so the link is undocumented and unverifiable.
findings.class: architecture limitation (documented split) + schema gap (no pointer)

resolution_options_assessed.A_extend_cuts: REJECTED - would clone the Remotion Cut interface (14+ scene types, dozens of props) into a public JSON Schema and force lockstep maintenance with Explainer.tsx. Highest churn, highest breakage risk.
resolution_options_assessed.B_governed_component_props_structure: PARTIAL - a typed props block inside edit_decisions duplicates the composition JSON that composition_validator and _remotion_render already consume by path.
resolution_options_assessed.C_keep_props_outside: CLOSEST TO TODAY - what the compose-director already prescribes, but leaves the artifact silent about the render input.
resolution_options_assessed.D_repository_intended: SELECTED - the repository already intends the split: composition JSON under remotion-composer/public/demo-props/<name>.json, validated by composition_validator and rendered via _remotion_render(composition_data). The atelier path shows the intended pattern for referencing an external render input: a small declared block (`bespoke` with entry/composition_id/art_direction, required when composition_mode='atelier').

findings.smallest_fix: Mirror the `bespoke` precedent for templated mode: add an OPTIONAL `templated` block (or single `composition_props_path` string) to edit_decisions recording the composition JSON path (plus optional sha256), and have video_compose load it when `edit_decisions.cuts` carry no scene props. Keeps cuts strict, makes the render input auditable, and matches the existing architecture instead of inventing one.
findings.backward_compat_risk: none if optional and additive; it is a public schema addition, so it must be versioned/announced. Existing projects that pass composition_data directly keep working unchanged.
tests: schema: edit_decisions with the new optional field validates; without it still validates
tool: when the pointer is present and cuts lack props, video_compose loads the props file and renders
governance: recorded path's sha256 matches the file actually rendered

findings.title: render_report / final_review record the superseded file size
findings.root_cause: Both were written with the measurements taken after the FIRST subtitle burn (6,886,991 bytes / 1,870,109 bps). The corrected re-burn replaced final.mp4 (7,387,202 bytes / 2,005,938 bps) and the artifacts were not re-measured.
findings.class: process/reporting defect (agent), not a repository bug
findings.evidence: BASELINE.json erratum ERR-1; re-probe of the delivered file.
findings.smallest_fix: Owner-approved correction write of the two artifacts (and the compose checkpoint) with the true size/bitrate, leaving all other values unchanged. Not performed - the freeze instruction forbids rewriting approved artifacts.
tests: compose-stage assertion that render_report.outputs[].file_size_bytes equals the on-disk size of the delivered file

findings.title: Playbook-derived theme is silently ignored for four playbook names
files: remotion-composer/src/Root.tsx (resolveTheme: named THEMES preset wins over themeConfig)
findings.root_cause: resolveTheme checks props.theme/props.playbook against the hardcoded THEMES map FIRST and returns the preset, ignoring the themeConfig that _build_theme_from_playbook derives from the playbook YAML. THEMES contains clean-professional, flat-motion-graphics, minimalist-diagram, anime-ghibli. Any project using one of those playbook names renders with the baked-in preset, so playbook palette edits never reach Remotion.
findings.class: architecture/implementation mismatch (discovered during this investigation, not in the original eight)
findings.evidence: premium-minimalist is NOT a preset, which is the only reason the injected themeConfig took effect in this validation run.
findings.smallest_fix: Invert the precedence when an explicit themeConfig is supplied: themeConfig (derived from the playbook YAML) should win, with the named preset as the fallback for callers that pass only a name.
findings.backward_compat_risk: medium-visible: projects using those four playbook names would start rendering with YAML-derived colours instead of the presets. Needs an explicit owner decision; a per-call opt-in flag is the conservative variant.
findings.dark_projects_affected: yes - flat-motion-graphics and anime-ghibli are both preset names
tests: unit: themeConfig supplied + preset name -> themeConfig wins
golden: name-only callers unchanged

light_theme_exposure_note: Two of the four built-in presets are already light (clean-professional #FFFFFF, minimalist-diagram #FAFAFA). E1 and E3 therefore already affect any existing project using those presets with stat_card subtitles, section_title, stat_reveal or hero_title - the defects are not exotic to premium-minimalist.
